title: Classifying noncompact groups over Hausdorff bases
statement: Construct a category of principal bundles over Hausdorff bases and universal objects that agree with ordinary bundles over completely regular bases while retaining characteristic information about a noncompact linear Lie group beyond the ordinary homotopy type of \(BG\).
status: As of November 2026, the specified linear-group programme is answered by \citet[\S\S1--2 and4]{gelfandfuchs1967topology}. The more general elementary-object formulation is treated by \citet[Theorems1--2]{gelfandfuchs1968classifying}, with stronger axioms than the notebook sketch.

title: Common fixed and periodic points of commuting interval maps
statement: Do two commuting continuous maps \([0,1]\to[0,1]\) necessarily share a fixed point? The accompanying differentiable statement asks for a fixed point of one map that is periodic for the other.
status: As of November 2026, the common-fixed-point assertion is false: the Boyce and Huneke counterexamples circulated in1967 and appeared in print in1969. A \(C^1\) map commuting with a continuous map has the fixed/periodic point described by Schwartz1965. The latter precise formulation was checked indirectly in \citet[Introduction]{alikhanikoopaei1998commuting}. This index entry does not add the different all-continuous common-periodic-point conjecture, which the notebook does not ask.

title: Metric classification of hyperbolic two-torus automorphisms
statement: When are two hyperbolic automorphisms of \(\mathbb T^2\), with Haar probability, isomorphic by an invertible measure-preserving conjugacy modulo zero?
status: As of November 2026, equality of entropy is necessary and sufficient by \citet[Main Theorem]{adlerweiss1967entropy}. The paper was communicated24April1967 and publishedJune1967, before both notebook occurrences. The four-block recoding and geometric component refinement in these notes match its proof exactly.

title: Algebraic classification of Anosov diffeomorphisms
statement: Is every Anosov diffeomorphism of a compact connected manifold topologically conjugate to an affine Anosov automorphism of an infranilmanifold?
status: As of November 2026, the general conjecture remains open. The known infranilmanifold case is the Franks--Manning theorem; the two-torus case is proved in \citet[Theorem5.2]{sinai1968markov}. See the precise conjecture and known case in \citet[Conjecture2.3, Theorem2.4]{spatzier2016rigidity} and its still-conjectural status in \citet[\S1, Background]{damjanovic2026symmetries}.

title: The unextended semisimple Gelfand--Kirillov conjecture
statement: For a complex semisimple Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\), is \(\operatorname{Frac}U(\mathfrak g)\) isomorphic to \(D_{|\Phi^+|,\operatorname{rank}\mathfrak g}\) without extending the centre?
status: November 2026: false in general by Premet (2009 preprint; 2010 publication), true for type A. The cited 2013 source leaves C and G2 open; no later exact resolution was verified. The 1969 theorem after central extension is a different assertion.

title: Automorphisms of Weyl division rings
statement: Describe the automorphism groups of Weyl division rings; in the present occurrence, determine \(\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Frac}A_1(\mathbb C)\), keeping polynomial algebra automorphisms and rational-subfield stabilizers distinct.
status: November 2026: no complete description was found in this audit; Dumas explicitly records the full automorphism-group question as open. The known stabilizer of \(\mathbb C(q)\) consists of lifted fractional-linear maps and rational shears. Lauritzen--Thomsen's October/November 2026 theorem on equality of left/right indices is a different result and does not settle the automorphism classification.

title: A universal family for the elliptic moduli problem
statement: Does an ordinary complex analytic parameter space represent all pointed elliptic families up to isomorphism, and what construction retains a universal family when this fails?
status: November 2026: the unrigidified family functor is not represented by the coarse j-line. A full homology marking gives the upper-half-plane universal family; the quotient stack or Mumford moduli site retains automorphisms. These facts were already established before the seminar.

title: The pointwise hyperbolic circle remainder
statement: Fix a cofinite Fuchsian group \(\Gamma<\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb R)\) and \(z,w\in\mathbb H^2\), and count group elements by \(N_\Gamma(R;z,w)=\#\{\gamma\in\Gamma:d(z,\gamma w)\le R\}\). Thus stabilizer multiplicities are included. Write this count as its full spectral main term (including eigenvalues below \(1/4\)) plus \(E(X;z,w)\), where \(X\asymp e^R\). Is \(E(X;z,w)=O_{\varepsilon,\Gamma,z,w}(X^{1/2+\varepsilon})\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\)? This is an explicitly weakened and qualified reconstruction of the notebook\textquoteright s square-root-remainder line, not its exact wording.
status: As of November 2026, unresolved in this general pointwise form in the searched literature. The 2025 preprint states the conjecture and proves a logarithmic improvement on the classical two-thirds bound for specified Heegner points, not the general square-root exponent \citep[Introduction and Theorem~1.1]{chatzakosetal2025hyperbolic}. The unspecified area-plus-boundary expression in the notebook is not certified as a true asymptotic expansion. The April 2026 preprint \citet[\S1.1, Theorem~1.2]{biro2026localsquare} gives a conditional local-square-mean improvement for the modular group, not a general pointwise bound.

title: Higher spectral asymptotics with a specified smoothing order
statement: For a positive scalar elliptic operator with smooth coefficients, determine the asymptotic coefficients and remainder of its diagonal Riesz means of order \(\alpha\). The occurrence asks first about \(\alpha=1\), then about formal expansions; these are distinguished from a pointwise unsmoothed expansion.
status: As of November 2026: solved in the appropriate finite-order smoothed sense already by \citet[Theorem~4.5 and pp.~215--216]{hormander1968spectral}; the general unsmoothed full-expansion reading is false, as the sphere in 1968-168.5 shows. No earlier exact problem identifier is supplied in the previous index.

title: The Langlands harmonic realization of the discrete series
statement: For a connected real semisimple group with finite centre and compact Cartan, determine the harmonic \(L^2\) Dolbeault cohomology of the homogeneous line bundle \(\mathcal L_\lambda\) on a fixed flag domain. The notes state the sufficiently regular case. The stronger literature formulation predicts vanishing for singular \(\lambda+\rho\), and otherwise a single nonzero degree \(q(\lambda+\rho)\) realizing the corresponding discrete series.
status: The notebook\textquotesingle s sufficiently regular theorem is established by Schmid\textquotesingle s work published in 1971; the 1976 paper proves the unrestricted \(L^2\) realization, as confirmed by the author\textquotesingle s ICM account, p.~204 \citep{schmid1980representations}. The all-weights formulation is an explicitly identified literature extension of this occurrence, not an additional conjecture transcribed from the notebook. The publisher metadata for both Annals papers was checked, and the exact early theorem was read in the Griffiths--Schmid paper and the 1971 Bourbaki exposition. The 1976 conclusion was checked against the author\textquotesingle s ICM account, not inferred merely from the title.

title: Finiteness for smooth homotopy tori
statement: For fixed \(n\geq5\), are there finitely many diffeomorphism classes of closed connected smooth manifolds homotopy equivalent to \(T^n\)? The continuation isolates the subproblem of finiteness within one smooth h-cobordism class.
status: Established. The 1969 fake-torus classification yields finitely many possibilities; the h-cobordism subproblem has the stronger answer one diffeomorphism type, by \(\operatorname{Wh}(\mathbb Z^n)=0\) and s-cobordism. Hsiang--Wall subsequently proved topological uniqueness in the high-dimensional range. None of these statements asserts smooth uniqueness or settles an unstated dimension-four problem.
